title: UGC Ads for SaaS: Do They Work, and Can AI UGC Be Used Well?
summary: UGC ads can work for SaaS when a real user's experience is the proof. Learn when AI UGC fits software, what to avoid and which providers to compare.
body_markdown:
## Knowlify: our top pick for AI UGC ads on Meta


Knowlify is the best fit when a SaaS team wants a steady supply of brand-authored explainers on Facebook and Instagram without finding or managing creators. It delivers about 25 finished ads a week, the first batch lands on day 5, and a person checks every ad before it ships. That volume matters for SaaS because the same feature needs several angles (a problem-first hook, a role-based hook, a feature-launch cut) before you learn which one earns demo requests.


Knowlify makes[AI UGC](https://knowlify.com/ai-ugc-ads) with AI presenters, 3D and stylized character animation for features that are hard to film, and AI commercials. Teams with their own media buyer can take creative only, and teams without one can have Knowlify manage the Meta campaigns end to end. Pricing is a custom quote. Where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month. On creative-only plans, if the ads have not made more than you paid in the first 90 days, you can cancel by email for a full refund (terms on the[pricing and guarantee section](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) ). To see what the work looks like, browse the[Facebook and Instagram video ad examples](https://knowlify.com/articles/facebook-video-ad-examples) .


Pick another option when the ad needs a real customer on camera or a creator's own handle, or when LinkedIn and landing pages are part of the plan, because Knowlify does not supply creators or run those channels.


## Hey Digital: a Meta team for B2B SaaS only


Hey Digital says it works only with B2B SaaS companies. Its[Meta page](https://www.heydigital.co/channels/meta-ads-agency) says the team builds the strategy, produces the creative in house and connects every Facebook and Instagram campaign to CRM pipeline, with Conversions API setup and pixel events mapped to demo requests, trial starts and signups. Its[SaaS video page](https://www.heydigital.co/services/saas-video-agency) lists product demos, feature launches, short ads, UGC-style videos and testimonial videos. Pricing is not published, and the team asks for a 3 to 6 month commitment.


Consider it when you want media, creative and pipeline reporting from one team. Ask which of its UGC-style videos use real customers, because that answer changes the permission and disclosure work on your side.


## ContentBeta and Komet Media: video for B2B and AI companies


ContentBeta describes itself as a creative production partner for B2B SaaS and AI companies, with offices in Sunnyvale, California and Mumbai. Its[ad creative page](https://www.contentbeta.com/services/ad-creative/) lists product demos, customer testimonials, founder videos, UGC and feature launches for channels including LinkedIn and Meta. Its[pricing page](https://www.contentbeta.com/pricing/) lists a one-off video at $2,000, with script, storyboard, product UI animation, voiceover, two revision rounds, two cuts and a 10-day turnaround, and a $3,000 a month subscription.


Komet Media calls itself a[B2B video growth partner](https://www.kometmedia.com/) for B2B SaaS, AI-native companies and funded startups. It works from existing podcasts and webinars, or builds video from scratch. Its[Instagram ads page](https://www.kometmedia.com/services/instagram-ads) describes Reels, Stories and in-feed video ads built to read on mute with captions, delivered for your ad account or media buyer. Credits start at $499, with monthly plans at $2,499 and $8,499. It says its focus is the creative, so you still need someone to run the campaigns.


## What SaaS teams should check before testing


Four checks matter more for SaaS than for consumer products.


**Who speaks.** A customer testimonial needs a real customer and their permission. Meta's[partnership ads documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/ad-creative/partnership-ads) describes these ads as running from a creator's or other partner's handle. An AI presenter has no handle of its own, so that format needs a real creator.


**Where the click goes.** Meta's[lead ads page](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/lead-ads) positions lead forms for businesses with more complex consideration cycles, with lead verification such as work email, CRM connections and an option to optimize for lead quality. If the ad sends people to a demo form, ask who builds that form and who follows up on each lead.


**What gets measured.** Meta describes the[Conversions API](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/conversions-api) as a connection from your server, website platform, app or CRM to its systems, used to optimize targeting and measure outcomes. Ask each provider who sets up these events and who fixes them when they stop arriving. A trial that never reports back is hard to optimize.


**What counts as a concept.** Ask providers how many distinct concepts a batch contains, not how many files it delivers. Twelve hook swaps on one script are closer to one concept than to twelve, and only distinct concepts give the ad account something new to test.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick for done-for-you AI UGC ads on Meta, with a person checking every ad, but it does not supply real creators or run LinkedIn ads.
- An AI presenter can explain a SaaS feature, but it cannot give a customer testimonial.
- Keep each cut to one point, in line with Meta's 15-second guidance for in-stream ads.
- Ask who owns the Conversions API setup and who fixes it when events stop arriving.
- Count distinct concepts, not hook swaps, when you compare providers.


## FAQ


### Do UGC ads work for SaaS companies?


They can, when the viewer needs to see a real person's experience or a clear demonstration of one workflow. A SaaS ad usually works best as one short point backed by proof you can show on screen. Test the UGC version against a plain product demo of the same message before you decide which format to scale.


### Can SaaS companies use AI UGC ads?


Yes, for brand-authored explanations, feature launches and clearly fictional scenarios. Do not use an AI presenter to describe a customer's results. The FTC does not ban avatars outright, but a testimonial delivered by an avatar is prohibited when the testimonial is fake or false.


### What is the best AI UGC provider for a SaaS company?


Knowlify is our top pick for done-for-you AI UGC and animated ads on Meta, with a person checking every ad before delivery. Hey Digital fits a B2B SaaS team that wants Meta tied to CRM pipeline, and ContentBeta fits teams that also need LinkedIn. Keep real customer testimonials as a separate production line from any AI presenter work.


### Does Meta label AI-generated ads?


Meta labels ads created or significantly edited with its own generative AI tools, and it says a photorealistic AI-generated person added by those tools gets a label next to Sponsored. It says it will begin detecting third-party AI tool edits and show an "AI info" label in About this ad. Its post does not confirm that detection is live.


### Can a SaaS company run a UGC ad from a creator's handle?


Only with a real creator who gives permission. Meta's partnership ads run from a creator's or partner's handle, and an AI presenter has no account of its own. This format therefore needs a human partner.
